title: RECIST 1.1: Simplified Framework for Response Assessment
summary: Practical guide to Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST 1.1). Standardized method for measuring tumor response to treatment based on changes in lesion size and emergence of new lesions.

content.text: RECIST 1.1: Response Assessment in Solid Tumors

RECIST 1.1 is the international standard for assessing tumor response to treatment in solid tumors. It provides objective, reproducible criteria for classifying response based on changes in tumor measurement.

items: Based on measurement of selected lesions over time (not all lesions measured)
Requires baseline imaging for comparison
Uses specific size thresholds to define response categories
Incorporates appearance of new lesions as indicator of progression
Provides standardized language for clinical trial participation and clinical practice

content.text: Lesions selected at baseline for measurement and follow-up tracking.

items: Minimum of 1, maximum of 5 lesions per organ (typically ≤10 total)
Lesions must be ≥10 mm in longest diameter on CT/MRI or ≥20 mm on plain radiograph
Must be radiographically measurable (not cystic, fatty, or necrotic)
Should represent different organ sites if multifocal disease
Same lesions followed at each reassessment

content.text: All other lesions at baseline that do not meet measurability criteria but are documented.

items: Includes lesions <10 mm, cystic lesions, lytic bone lesions, pleural effusions
Not measured but described as present, unchanged, or absent
Assessed qualitatively rather than quantitatively
Their status affects overall response classification

content.text: Any lesion not present at baseline, including lesions in new anatomic sites.

items: Appearance of any new lesion is classified as progressive disease
Even a single new lesion overrides partial or stable response
Must be >10 mm to be classified as new (smaller lesions may be inflammatory)
All target lesions disappear (sum of diameters = 0)
No new lesions appear
Non-target lesions resolved or unchanged
≥30% decrease in sum of target lesion diameters (compared to baseline)
No new lesions
Non-target lesions may regress or remain unchanged
<30% decrease AND <20% increase in sum of target lesion diameters
No new lesions
Non-target lesions remain stable or resolve
≥20% increase in sum of target lesion diameters (compared to baseline or nadir), OR
Any new lesion appears, OR
Non-target lesions worsen with appearance of new or unequivocal progression

content.text: Step-by-step walkthrough of RECIST response calculation.
A patient with metastatic lung cancer has baseline CT showing: (1) left upper lobe mass 32 mm, (2) right lower lobe mass 28 mm, (3) liver lesion 15 mm, (4) adrenal lesion 12 mm.
Selected target lesions: #1 (32 mm) and #2 (28 mm) = baseline sum 60 mm
After 2 cycles of chemotherapy, repeat CT shows: (1) left mass 22 mm, (2) right mass 20 mm, (3) liver unchanged, (4) adrenal unchanged, (5) new small hepatic lesion 8 mm

items: Current sum of target lesions: 22 + 20 = 42 mm
Change from baseline: (42 - 60) / 60 × 100 = -30%
Assessment: ≥30% decrease = meets criteria for PR
However: New liver lesion (8 mm) is <10 mm, so interpreted as uncertain/inflammatory
Final Response: Partial Response (PR)

content.text: If a selected target lesion becomes difficult to measure (due to location change, treatment effect, or image quality), it may be replaced with a different lesion at baseline if one exists. This should be documented.

Cystic changes or necrosis within a lesion may reduce density but increase overall size. RECIST measures longest diameter regardless of internal composition, so size may appear stable or increase despite good treatment effect.
Lytic bone lesions may show sclerotic (hardened) response to treatment, which is favorable but not measurable by RECIST. These should be documented but are typically classified as non-target lesions.

items: Lymphomas: Use RECIST-L (modified for lymph node measurement)
Metastatic bone disease: May use bone response criteria
Immunotherapy: Some responses are atypical (may appear to worsen before improving); use iRECIST or irRECIST
Cystic or necrotic tumors: May require modified criteria
RECIST provides standardized, objective method for response assessment
Requires baseline imaging and consistent measurement technique
Response classification is based on target lesions + new lesions + non-target status
Appearance of new lesion = progressive disease regardless of target lesion response
Always document which lesions were selected, their baseline sizes, and current sizes
